Application of Cathode Ray Oscilloscope by Field, With Types of CRO

The main application of cathode ray oscilloscope work is to display a voltage waveform against time so that amplitude, time period, frequency, phase and distortion can be read directly from the screen. The table below groups the common uses by field.

FieldTypical CRO application
Electronics labsChecking amplifier gain, clipping and distortion
CommunicationViewing AM and FM modulation, pulses and noise
Power electronicsViewing rectifier ripple and inverter switching waveforms
Digital circuitsChecking clock signals, rise time and timing between channels
Phase and frequency workLissajous patterns using X Y mode
Medical and serviceDisplaying ECG type signals and fault finding in TV and radio circuits

Types of CRO in Brief

The usual types of CRO are the analog CRO, the dual beam CRO (two electron beams), the dual trace CRO (one beam switched between two inputs), the sampling CRO for very high frequency repetitive signals, the analog storage CRO and the digital storage oscilloscope, which converts the signal to digital data and can hold a trace on screen.

Key Advantages of CRO

The main advantages of CRO are real time waveform display, very high input impedance so the circuit is hardly loaded, wide bandwidth, the ability to compare two signals at once and stable traces through triggering. Its limits are a small screen, need for careful calibration and, for analog types, no storage of one time events.
